3: /// <summary>
4: /// TR-MCP-NUKE-019 (AC-1): Contract cases and assertions for <see cref="IIntegrationLaneFilter"/>. The expected filters
5: /// come from the acceptance criterion; a small evaluator of the trait grammar the lane uses (terms joined by '&',
6: /// Name=Value requires the trait, Name!=Value is met by any other value or by no trait) checks what each filter
7: /// selects for an untagged case, an own-host case, an other-host case and a non-integration case. The same
8: /// assertions run against the scripted filter (BDPv4 mock gate), wrong filters (negative controls), and the
9: /// production filter.
10: /// </summary>
11: internal static class IntegrationLaneFilterContract
12: {
13:     /// <summary>Every host name, in the order the contract checks them.</summary>
14:     internal static readonly string[] HostNames = ["windows", "linux"];
15: 
16:     /// <summary>Parses a contract host name.</summary>
17:     /// <param name="hostName">windows or linux.</param>
18:     internal static IntegrationLaneHost Parse(string hostName) => hostName switch
19:     {
20:         "windows" => IntegrationLaneHost.Windows,
21:         "linux" => IntegrationLaneHost.Linux,
22:         _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(hostName), hostName, "Unknown contract host."),
23:     };
24: 
25:     /// <summary>The filter TR-MCP-NUKE-019 AC-1 requires for <paramref name="host"/>.</summary>
26:     /// <param name="host">Host the lane runs on.</param>
27:     internal static string ExpectedFilter(IntegrationLaneHost host) => host switch
28:     {
29:         IntegrationLaneHost.Windows => "Category=Integration&Platform!=Linux",
30:         IntegrationLaneHost.Linux => "Category=Integration&Platform!=Windows",
31:         _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(host), host, "Unknown host."),
32:     };
33: 
34:     /// <summary>Asserts that <paramref name="filter"/> meets the contract for the named host.</summary>
35:     /// <param name="hostName">windows or linux.</param>
36:     /// <param name="filter">Filter under test.</param>
37:     internal static void AssertHost(string hostName, IIntegrationLaneFilter filter)
38:     {
39:         var host = Parse(hostName);
40:         var actual = filter.Compose(host);
41: 
42:         Assert.Equal(ExpectedFilter(host), actual);
43:         AssertSelection(host, actual);
44:     }
45: 
46:     /// <summary>
47:     /// Asserts what <paramref name="filter"/> selects on <paramref name="host"/>: untagged and own-host integration
48:     /// cases run; other-host and non-integration cases do not. Independent of the exact filter text, so the negative
49:     /// controls prove each of these assertions rejects a wrong filter on its own.
50:     /// </summary>
51:     /// <param name="host">Host the lane runs on.</param>
52:     /// <param name="filter">Filter text under test.</param>
53:     internal static void AssertSelection(IntegrationLaneHost host, string filter)
54:     {
55:         var own = host == IntegrationLaneHost.Windows ? "Windows" : "Linux";
56:         var other = host == IntegrationLaneHost.Windows ? "Linux" : "Windows";
57: 
58:         Assert.True(Selects(filter, category: "Integration", platform: null), "An untagged integration case must run on every host.");
59:         Assert.True(Selects(filter, category: "Integration", platform: own), $"A Platform={own} integration case must run on its own host.");
60:         Assert.False(Selects(filter, category: "Integration", platform: other), $"A Platform={other} integration case must not run on a {own} host.");
61:         Assert.False(Selects(filter, category: null, platform: null), "A case without Category=Integration must not run in the integration lane.");
62:     }
63: 
64:     /// <summary>Evaluates the '&'-joined Name=Value and Name!=Value terms against one case's traits.</summary>
65:     /// <param name="filter">Filter text.</param>
66:     /// <param name="category">The case's Category trait, or null.</param>
67:     /// <param name="platform">The case's Platform trait, or null.</param>
68:     internal static bool Selects(string filter, string? category, string? platform)
69:     {
70:         var traits = new Dictionary<string, string?>(StringComparer.Ordinal)
71:         {
72:             ["Category"] = category,
73:             ["Platform"] = platform,
74:         };
75:         foreach (var term in filter.Split('&', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries | StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries))
76:         {
77:             var negated = term.Contains("!=", StringComparison.Ordinal);
78:             var parts = term.Split(negated ? "!=" : "=", 2, StringSplitOptions.TrimEntries);
79:             if (parts.Length != 2 || !traits.TryGetValue(parts[0], out var value))
80:             {
81:                 throw new FormatException($"Unsupported filter term '{term}'.");
82:             }
83: 
84:             var equal = string.Equals(value, parts[1], StringComparison.Ordinal);
85:             if (negated ? equal : !equal)
86:             {
87:                 return false;
88:             }
89:         }
90: 
91:         return true;
92:     }
93: }

3: /// <summary>
4: /// TR-MCP-NUKE-019 (AC-1), BDPv4 mock gate: proves the <see cref="IntegrationLaneFilterContract"/> assertions accept a
5: /// scripted filter that produces the contract-derived filters, and reject deliberately wrong filters (negative
6: /// controls), before any production filter code is written.
7: /// </summary>
8: public sealed class IntegrationLaneFilterMockGateTests
9: {
10:     /// <summary>TR-MCP-NUKE-019: every host passes against the scripted filter.</summary>
11:     /// <param name="host">Host name from <see cref="IntegrationLaneFilterContract.HostNames"/>.</param>
12:     [Theory]
13:     [InlineData("windows")]
14:     [InlineData("linux")]
15:     public void ScriptedFilter_PassesHost(string host)
16:         => IntegrationLaneFilterContract.AssertHost(host, new ScriptedFilter(Fault.None));
17: 
18:     /// <summary>TR-MCP-NUKE-019: the theory above covers every contract host.</summary>
19:     [Fact]
20:     public void ScriptedFilterTheory_CoversEveryHost()
21:         => Assert.Equal(2, IntegrationLaneFilterContract.HostNames.Length);
22: 
23:     /// <summary>
24:     /// TR-MCP-NUKE-019 negative controls: each wrong filter is rejected (the other host's cases admitted, untagged
25:     /// cases dropped, hosts swapped, the Category=Integration term dropped).
26:     /// </summary>
27:     /// <param name="host">Host the fault is checked on.</param>
28:     /// <param name="fault">Injected fault.</param>
29:     [Theory]
30:     [InlineData("windows", Fault.AdmitsOtherHost)]
31:     [InlineData("linux", Fault.AdmitsOtherHost)]
32:     [InlineData("windows", Fault.DropsUntagged)]
33:     [InlineData("linux", Fault.DropsUntagged)]
34:     [InlineData("windows", Fault.SwapsHosts)]
35:     [InlineData("linux", Fault.SwapsHosts)]
36:     [InlineData("windows", Fault.DropsCategory)]
37:     [InlineData("linux", Fault.DropsCategory)]
38:     public void WrongFilter_IsRejected(string host, Fault fault)
39:         => Assert.ThrowsAny<Xunit.Sdk.XunitException>(
40:             () => IntegrationLaneFilterContract.AssertHost(host, new ScriptedFilter(fault)));
41: 
42:     /// <summary>
43:     /// TR-MCP-NUKE-019 negative controls: the selection assertions alone, without the exact-text check, reject each
44:     /// wrong filter. Each fault breaks a different assertion (other host admitted, untagged dropped, own host
45:     /// excluded, non-integration admitted), so every selection assertion is shown to discriminate.
46:     /// </summary>
47:     /// <param name="host">Host the fault is checked on.</param>
48:     /// <param name="fault">Injected fault.</param>
49:     [Theory]
50:     [InlineData("windows", Fault.AdmitsOtherHost)]
51:     [InlineData("linux", Fault.AdmitsOtherHost)]
52:     [InlineData("windows", Fault.DropsUntagged)]
53:     [InlineData("linux", Fault.DropsUntagged)]
54:     [InlineData("windows", Fault.SwapsHosts)]
55:     [InlineData("linux", Fault.SwapsHosts)]
56:     [InlineData("windows", Fault.DropsCategory)]
57:     [InlineData("linux", Fault.DropsCategory)]
58:     public void WrongFilter_FailsSelection(string host, Fault fault)
59:     {
60:         var parsed = IntegrationLaneFilterContract.Parse(host);
61:         var filter = new ScriptedFilter(fault).Compose(parsed);
62:         Assert.ThrowsAny<Xunit.Sdk.XunitException>(() => IntegrationLaneFilterContract.AssertSelection(parsed, filter));
63:     }
64: 
65:     /// <summary>TR-MCP-NUKE-019: the contract evaluator refuses a term it cannot read instead of guessing.</summary>
66:     /// <param name="filter">Filter with an unsupported term.</param>
67:     [Theory]
68:     [InlineData("Category~Integration")]
69:     [InlineData("Category=Integration&Owner!=Linux")]
70:     public void Evaluator_RejectsUnsupportedTerm(string filter)
71:         => Assert.Throws<FormatException>(() => IntegrationLaneFilterContract.Selects(filter, "Integration", null));
72: 
73:     /// <summary>Faults injected into the scripted filter for negative controls.</summary>
74:     public enum Fault
75:     {
76:         /// <summary>No fault: the contract-derived filter.</summary>
77:         None,
78: 
79:         /// <summary>Selects every integration case, including the other host's.</summary>
80:         AdmitsOtherHost,
81: 
82:         /// <summary>Selects only cases tagged for the host, dropping untagged integration cases.</summary>
83:         DropsUntagged,
84: 
85:         /// <summary>Excludes the host's own cases instead of the other host's.</summary>
86:         SwapsHosts,
87: 
88:         /// <summary>Drops the Category=Integration term.</summary>
89:         DropsCategory,
90:     }
91: 
92:     /// <summary>Scripted filter: the contract-derived filters, with an optional injected fault.</summary>
93:     private sealed class ScriptedFilter(Fault fault) : IIntegrationLaneFilter
94:     {
95:         /// <inheritdoc />
96:         public string Compose(IntegrationLaneHost host)
97:         {
98:             var own = host == IntegrationLaneHost.Windows ? "Windows" : "Linux";
99:             var other = host == IntegrationLaneHost.Windows ? "Linux" : "Windows";
100:             return fault switch
101:             {
102:                 Fault.None => $"Category=Integration&Platform!={other}",
103:                 Fault.AdmitsOtherHost => "Category=Integration",
104:                 Fault.DropsUntagged => $"Category=Integration&Platform={own}",
105:                 Fault.SwapsHosts => $"Category=Integration&Platform!={own}",
106:                 Fault.DropsCategory => $"Platform!={other}",
107:                 _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(fault), fault, "Unknown fault."),
108:             };
109:         }
110:     }
111: }

3: /// <summary>
4: /// TR-MCP-NUKE-019 (AC-5): contract scenarios and assertions for <see cref="IIntegrationLanePrecondition"/>. The
5: /// expected outcomes come from the criterion: on Windows the lane runs only from an interactive desktop session
6: /// and otherwise fails before any test, naming the missing session; on Linux no session requirement applies. The
7: /// same assertions run against the scripted precondition (BDPv4 mock gate), wrong preconditions (negative
8: /// controls), and the production precondition.
9: /// </summary>
10: internal static class IntegrationLanePreconditionContract
11: {
12:     /// <summary>Every scenario name, in the order the contract checks them.</summary>
13:     internal static readonly string[] ScenarioNames =
14:     [
15:         "windows-interactive",
16:         "windows-noninteractive",
17:         "linux-interactive",
18:         "linux-noninteractive",
19:     ];
20: 
21:     /// <summary>Asserts that <paramref name="precondition"/> meets the named scenario.</summary>
22:     /// <param name="scenario">Scenario name from <see cref="ScenarioNames"/>.</param>
23:     /// <param name="precondition">Precondition under test.</param>
24:     internal static void AssertScenario(string scenario, IIntegrationLanePrecondition precondition)
25:     {
26:         var (host, interactive, mayRun) = scenario switch
27:         {
28:             "windows-interactive" => (IntegrationLaneHost.Windows, true, true),
29:             "windows-noninteractive" => (IntegrationLaneHost.Windows, false, false),
30:             "linux-interactive" => (IntegrationLaneHost.Linux, true, true),
31:             "linux-noninteractive" => (IntegrationLaneHost.Linux, false, true),
32:             _ => throw new ArgumentOutOfRangeException(nameof(scenario), scenario, "Unknown contract scenario."),
33:         };
34: 
35:         var readiness = precondition.Evaluate(host, interactive);
36: 
37:         Assert.Equal(mayRun, readiness.CanRun);
38:         if (mayRun)
39:         {
40:             Assert.Null(readiness.FailureMessage);
41:             return;
42:         }
43: 
44:         Assert.False(string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(readiness.FailureMessage), "A lane that cannot run must say why instead of stopping silently.");
45:         Assert.Contains("interactive desktop session", readiness.FailureMessage, StringComparison.Ordinal);
46:         Assert.Contains("MigrationIntegrationTests", readiness.FailureMessage, StringComparison.Ordinal);
47:     }
48: }

3: /// <summary>
4: /// TR-MCP-NUKE-019 (AC-5), BDPv4 mock gate: proves the <see cref="IntegrationLanePreconditionContract"/> assertions
5: /// accept a scripted precondition that produces the criterion's outcomes, and reject deliberately wrong
6: /// preconditions (negative controls), before any production precondition code is written.
7: /// </summary>
8: public sealed class IntegrationLanePreconditionMockGateTests
9: {
10:     /// <summary>TR-MCP-NUKE-019 AC-5: every scenario passes against the scripted precondition.</summary>
11:     /// <param name="scenario">Scenario name from <see cref="IntegrationLanePreconditionContract.ScenarioNames"/>.</param>
12:     [Theory]
13:     [InlineData("windows-interactive")]
14:     [InlineData("windows-noninteractive")]
15:     [InlineData("linux-interactive")]
16:     [InlineData("linux-noninteractive")]
17:     public void ScriptedPrecondition_PassesScenario(string scenario)
18:         => IntegrationLanePreconditionContract.AssertScenario(scenario, new ScriptedPrecondition(Fault.None));
19: 
20:     /// <summary>TR-MCP-NUKE-019 AC-5: the theory above covers every contract scenario.</summary>
21:     [Fact]
22:     public void ScriptedTheory_CoversEveryScenario()
23:         => Assert.Equal(4, IntegrationLanePreconditionContract.ScenarioNames.Length);
24: 
25:     /// <summary>
26:     /// TR-MCP-NUKE-019 AC-5 negative controls: a precondition that runs a non-interactive Windows session, stops
27:     /// without a message (a silent skip), names no session in its message, or blocks a Linux host, is rejected.
28:     /// </summary>
29:     /// <param name="scenario">Scenario the fault breaks.</param>
30:     /// <param name="fault">Injected fault.</param>
31:     [Theory]
32:     [InlineData("windows-noninteractive", Fault.RunsWhenNonInteractive)]
33:     [InlineData("windows-noninteractive", Fault.StopsSilently)]
34:     [InlineData("windows-noninteractive", Fault.MessageOmitsSession)]
35:     [InlineData("linux-noninteractive", Fault.BlocksLinux)]
36:     public void WrongPrecondition_IsRejected(string scenario, Fault fault)
37:         => Assert.ThrowsAny<Xunit.Sdk.XunitException>(
38:             () => IntegrationLanePreconditionContract.AssertScenario(scenario, new ScriptedPrecondition(fault)));
39: 
40:     /// <summary>Faults injected into the scripted precondition for negative controls.</summary>
41:     public enum Fault
42:     {
43:         /// <summary>No fault: the criterion's outcomes.</summary>
44:         None,
45: 
46:         /// <summary>Lets a non-interactive Windows session run the lane.</summary>
47:         RunsWhenNonInteractive,
48: 
49:         /// <summary>Refuses the lane but gives no message, so the run would stop silently.</summary>
50:         StopsSilently,
51: 
52:         /// <summary>Refuses the lane with a message that does not name the missing session.</summary>
53:         MessageOmitsSession,
54: 
55:         /// <summary>Applies the Windows session requirement to a Linux host.</summary>
56:         BlocksLinux,
57:     }
58: 
59:     /// <summary>Scripted precondition: the criterion's outcomes, with an optional injected fault.</summary>
60:     private sealed class ScriptedPrecondition(Fault fault) : IIntegrationLanePrecondition
61:     {
62:         private const string Message = "MigrationIntegrationTests needs an interactive desktop session on Windows.";
63: 
64:         /// <inheritdoc />
65:         public IntegrationLaneReadiness Evaluate(IntegrationLaneHost host, bool userInteractive)
66:         {
67:             if (fault == Fault.BlocksLinux && !userInteractive)
68:                 return new IntegrationLaneReadiness(false, Message);
69:             if (host != IntegrationLaneHost.Windows || userInteractive)
70:                 return new IntegrationLaneReadiness(true, null);
71: 
72:             return fault switch
73:             {
74:                 Fault.RunsWhenNonInteractive => new IntegrationLaneReadiness(true, null),
75:                 Fault.StopsSilently => new IntegrationLaneReadiness(false, null),
76:                 Fault.MessageOmitsSession => new IntegrationLaneReadiness(false, "MigrationIntegrationTests cannot run here."),
77:                 _ => new IntegrationLaneReadiness(false, Message),
78:             };
79:         }
80:     }
81: }
